comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the body-cap truncation drops the `release-draft-owner` marker — truncated drafts become un-reclaimable**

Both writers stamp the draft-ownership marker at the **end** of the notes file and *then* call the cap helper, which truncates from the tail:

```bash
# release_lazy_draft.sh:67 / release_attach_or_create.sh:103
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >> "$notes"
# ... then (line 73 / 108):
bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes_cap.sh" "$notes"
```

`release_notes_cap.sh` keeps the first ~120 KB and cuts the tail — verified with a 141 KB body + marker: after the cap the marker is gone (`grep -c 'release-draft-owner'` → 0). Every consumer matches the marker **in the release body**:

- `scripts/release_draft_guard.sh:60-64` — on a leg failure after the create, owner resolves to `<unmarked>` ≠ identity → the guard refuses to delete its own draft (warning, exit 0);
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:128` — unmarked body + PAT author (the legs run with `GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT`; per gh-2008 the API author is the human owner, the marker is "the only ownership proof") → **human** bucket → kept and merely listed, never reclaimed; the fresh gh-2318 reclaim also requires a well-formed marker;
- `scripts/release_draft_dedupe.sh:73` — twin-draft dedupe requires `contains("release-draft-owner: " + $run)`.

This is not a rare path: the curated `## Unreleased` section is ~131 KB and archiving is deferred (your own Notes), so **every upcoming release body truncates**. Before this PR an over-cap create failed (no draft existed); after it the create succeeds with an unmarked body — and a leg dying mid-upload leaves a permanently orphaned draft, exactly the hazard `release_lazy_draft.sh`'s own identity-validation comment warns about ("a forever-orphaned draft", gh-282: a draft must be published or deleted, never orphaned).

**Fix (either, ~2 lines):** call `release_notes_cap.sh` **before** appending the owner marker in both writers (bounded body + marker ≈ 120.1 KB < the 125k API cap), or teach the truncation cut to preserve a trailing `<!-- release-draft-owner: ... -->` line. The attach-path site (`release_attach_or_create.sh:108`) needs the same ordering fix.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
# Thread: `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh:73` — body-cap truncation drops the `release-draft-owner` marker

**Severity**: ⚠️ IMPORTANT — **fixed in code** (commits `eb3d56b604` + `a2d531fdf3`, pushed to `ai/gh-2337`).

## Fix

Took fix option 1 (the ordering swap) at **both** writer sites — `release_lazy_draft.sh` and `release_attach_or_create.sh` — so the created draft body is always bounded-notes **plus** the trailing owner marker:

```bash
# release_lazy_draft.sh (attach twin mirrored in release_attach_or_create.sh)
bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes_cap.sh" "$notes_file"   # cap FIRST — truncation cuts from the tail
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: $identity -->"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes_file" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >>"$notes_file"
```

Rationale documented inline at both sites: a pre-stamped marker is cut off by the tail-truncation, leaving a draft `release_draft_guard.sh` resolves as `<unmarked>` and refuses to reclaim, that `sweep_stale_drafts.sh` buckets human (the legs run with `GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT`) and keeps, and that `release_draft_dedupe.sh` ignores — the forever-orphaned-draft shape (gh-282). Bounded body (≤ 120,000 bytes) + the ~70-byte marker stays well under the 125,000-character API cap, so the swap does not re-open the HTTP 422 this PR fixes (`release_notes_cap.sh`'s own header already budgeted "the slack also absorbs the marker line itself").

## TDD evidence

- RED (before the fix): two new fixture tests reproduced your exact experiment — an over-cap body (~131 KB, the production curated-`## Unreleased` shape) created a draft whose `--notes-file` capture contained **no** `release-draft-owner` marker (`…(truncated — 12877 bytes dropped…` tail only):
  - `test/release_lazy_draft_mint_test.dart` — "gh-2337 rework: an over-cap lazy draft body still carries the release-draft-owner marker" (new `seedOversizeChangelog` fixture knob seeds a ~132 KB curated Unreleased CHANGELOG, exercising `release_notes.sh` preference 1b end-to-end).
  - `test/release_attach_or_create_mint_test.dart` — "gh-2337 rework: the bounded attach body still carries the release-draft-owner marker".
- GREEN (after the fix): both pass; both assert the captured create body carries `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>` **and** stays ≤ 125,000 bytes. The pre-existing "over-cap release-notes.md is bounded before the create" test was tightened to the new contract: body-minus-marker ≤ 120,000 (the bounded ceiling) and full notes ≤ 125,000 (the API cap).
- Full touched-file surface green: 22 tests in the three mint/cap test files; 167 tests across the release/guard surface (`release_hygiene`, `release_draft_dedupe`, `release_stale_draft_reclaim`, `release_empty_latest_guard`, `release_publish_immutability`, `ci_release_dedupe_guard`, `ci_release_pending_guard`). `bash -n` + `shellcheck` clean on all three scripts; `dart analyze` + `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` clean on the touched test files.

## Digest pickup (same release surface)

The 4 digit-dropped run-id comment spots (`468064719` → `44680647719`) are corrected in `release_lazy_draft.sh`, `release_attach_or_create.sh`, and `release_notes_cap.sh`. The `test/ci_2337_macos_size_floor_test.dart` comment/test-name digit-drops are left for triage (outside the files this fix touches, per the same-files-only opportunistic bound; the code constants there are already correct).

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: Root-cause fix is on-target for gh-2337 (release-body cap + both mac size floors, documented gh-2088-style reseed) and well tested — 26 touched tests green, `bash -n`/`shellcheck` clean, `dart format`/`analyze` clean. One real defect: the new truncation silently strips the `release-draft-owner` marker the draft guard, sweeper and dedupe all match on.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ Both writers append the ownership marker **before** `release_notes_cap.sh` truncates the tail — any over-cap body (the ~131 KB curated `## Unreleased` will truncate on every train until archived) creates a marker-less draft: the lifecycle guard refuses to reclaim it, the sweeper buckets it human (PAT author) and keeps it, dedupe ignores it — a forever-orphaned draft on the failure path gh-282 exists to prevent.

**Next Steps**:
1. Cap the notes **before** appending the marker (swap the order in `release_lazy_draft.sh` and `release_attach_or_create.sh`; bounded body + marker ≈ 120.1 KB < the 125k cap), or preserve the marker line in the truncation cut.
2. Digest (no threads): mangled run id `468064719` in 4 script comment spots and `TOTAL 811153036` / `74701116` digit-drops in `test/ci_2337_macos_size_floor_test.dart` comments/test name — real values `44680647719` / `811153036` / `74701116` (tests use the correct ones; comments only).
3. Digest: a transient `gh release view` failure in the new race re-view reds a race-won leg (safe direction — fails loud); `release_notes_cap.sh` with a cap below the marker reserve misbehaves via negative slice (unreachable from the two callers, default 120000).
